key_insight: An ion-pumped SrFeO$_{3-\delta}$ thin film can reversibly switch between brownmillerite and perovskite phases, enabling continuous analog control of optical transmittance and color.
engineering_relevance: This shows a low-power, nonvolatile electrochromic approach based on oxygen-ion motion that is compatible with oxide electronics and potentially silicon photonics.
method: Built an SrFeO$_{3-\delta}$ thin-film device that undergoes reversible oxygen-driven phase transitions.
Integrated an optically passive Al$_2$O$_3$ interference layer to amplify tunable optical response.
Used ion-induced structural and redox changes to modulate electronic structure and optical constants.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports pronounced, reversible changes in optical transmittance and color across the phase transition, supporting continuous optical modulation.
watch_item: Practical deployment may depend on maintaining fast, durable, and repeatable oxygen-ion switching without degradation over many cycles.
paper_title: Structure-driven analog optical control in ion-pumped SrFeO$_{3-δ}$ thin-film devices
